independentRemediationAttempts.sideEffectRootCause: NOT a bug. Verified via source (src/parser/source-parser.ts:568-586): FIGM-NEXT-03 (missing `export const revalidate`) is deliberately gated on `!hasUseClientDirective` — a Client Component legitimately does not need server route-segment revalidate config. Confirmed by reading the exact gating condition in source, not inferred.

genuineFindings.title: Bounded retry does not distinguish a permanent provider error from a transient one
genuineFindings.evidence: Forcing HF_MODEL to a nonexistent id and running the full pipeline made 3 real HTTP 400 calls (all identical failures) before giving up, instead of failing fast after the first.
genuineFindings.impact: Wastes latency/cost on a call that will deterministically fail every time; never produces an incorrect result — final state was correctly UNAVAILABLE with source unchanged.
genuineFindings.location: src/ai/ai-remediation-pipeline.ts — the early-break condition only recognizes "environment variable is not configured" / "No AI remediation provider is configured", not other permanent failures like an HTTP 400/404 model-not-found.

genuineFindings.title: Patch-scope safety heuristic can reject a correct AI fix on a very small fixture
genuineFindings.evidence: A verified-correct, minimal Qwen patch (add useMemo import + wrap one line) was rejected on a 4-line file because it crossed the 60%-changed-lines threshold once the file reached 6 total lines.
genuineFindings.impact: None on real project files (which are essentially never 4-6 lines); demonstrated here only because the canonical rule-catalog fixture is that small. The heuristic is doing exactly what it was designed to do (reject an implausibly large rewrite) — it just cannot distinguish "large ratio because the file is tiny" from "large ratio because the rewrite is excessive." No change made or recommended per the task's instruction not to alter production logic to satisfy a fixture.

genuineFindings.title: Fixing FIGM-NEXT-01 makes FIGM-NEXT-03 stop firing on the same file
genuineFindings.evidence: Confirmed via source.parser.ts:568-586 — FIGM-NEXT-03 is deliberately inapplicable once a file has a "use client" directive.
genuineFindings.impact: None — correct, intentional rule interaction, not violation-hiding.

finalVerdict.question: Can the current FIGM system genuinely use Qwen3-Coder through the Hugging Face API as an AI remediation assistant, after FIGM detects a violation, and safely generate → validate → re-scan → verify a fix?
finalVerdict.scopeOfYes: Proven end-to-end with real, live, non-mocked network calls: detection → AI_ASSISTED routing → real Qwen3-Coder patch generation → in-memory sandbox validation (syntax/scope/TypeScript compile) → real FIGM re-scan → VERIFIED, for 3 different rules (FIGM-REACT-01, FIGM-REACT-08, FIGM-REACT-09) in realistic-sized fixtures, 3/3 successful. Provider routing definitively confirmed Qwen (never Claude) was used in every live call this session, with the Anthropic path preserved only as an unused fallback. Failure/safety paths (invalid model, invalid token, an undersized fixture triggering the scope heuristic) all degraded honestly to REJECT/UNAVAILABLE with the original source always left untouched — never a fabricated VERIFIED.
caveats: Only 3 of the 12 AI_ASSISTED-routed rules were live-API-tested end-to-end in this session (cost/time); the other 9 are architecturally routed the same way and share the same code path, but were not individually live-verified here.
The patch-scope safety heuristic can reject a correct AI patch on very small (<6 line) files — a real, demonstrated, working-as-designed limitation, not a failure of the Qwen integration itself.
A permanent provider error (e.g. an invalid model id) is retried 3x before giving up — a minor latency/cost inefficiency, not a correctness issue.
